segments: and took the two fortresses of 'Amm and Artah from the Arabs.
And the Romans spread out as far as Mabbugh (Hierapolis),
and the majority of its inhabitants fled to Aleppo.
For the hire of a camel from Mabbugh to Aleppo rose to eighty gold dinars.
And the Romans gained control over Mabbugh,
and they made a great slaughter in it,
and they destroyed its wall,
and with its stones they rebuilt the old fortress that was in it.
And because the Romans were numerous,
and there were no provisions for them from anywhere,
due to the Turks who were raiding between the borders,
famine grew severe among them.
And a pound of bread came to cost a dinar,
and six handfuls of barley a dinar.
And certain Ma'addite (Arab) Kalbites related:
"We killed a man from among the Romans,
and when we ripped open his belly,
we found whole grains of barley inside it."
And when news came to the king (Emperor):
"Afshin the Turk has entered Roman territory and conquered the city of Amorium,"
he placed guards in the new fortress that he had built in Mabbugh,
and he returned to the land of the Romans.
And in the year 1382 [of the Greeks = 1070/1071 AD],
462 of the Arabs [AH = 1069/1070 AD], there was a famine in Egypt,
to such a degree that human beings ate one another.
For in all Egypt, apart from three horses for the Caliph, none remained;
as for the rest,
horses, mules, and donkeys,
their owners ate them.
And a dog was sold for five dinars and ten zuzes,
and onions [were sold] by weight for a silver coin.
It is said
that on one of the days, when the Vizier dismounted from his mule
and went in to the Caliph,
three men came and snatched the mule from the hands of his servant,
and they slaughtered it and ate it.
And when the deed was made known to the Caliph,
he commanded, and those three men were impaled.
And at night others came
and took them down from the stakes,
and cut off slices of their flesh and went away.
And when morning dawned,
their stripped bones were found piled up beneath the stakes.
And not only over the common people,
but also over the palace did the famine {OCR?} prevail,
to the point that all the royal possessions were sold for reduced prices.
For ten pearls which weighed ten mitqals
were sold for four hundred dinars.
